documents.text:
George Frank Butler

George Frank Butler (born 1955) is an American physician known for his contributions to the field of cardiology. Early Life and Education

Butler was born in New York City, USA. He pursued his undergraduate degree in biology from the University of Rochester, graduating magna cum laude in 1977. [1] Following his undergraduate studies, Butler moved to the United Kingdom to attend Durham University, where he earned his Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree in 1982. [2]

Studies and Career

After completing his medical degree, Butler returned to the United States and began his residency at Columbia University Medical Center. He went on to specialize in cardiology, earning his fellowship from the American College of Cardiology in 1990. [3]

Butler's research focuses on the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. He has published numerous papers on the topic, including a seminal study on the effects of statins on cardiovascular health, published in the Journal of the American Medical Association in 2005. [4]
